paper.title: Nano-mechanical properties of Fe-Mn-Al-C lightweight steels
paper.paper_scope: Two duplex low-density steels, Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni and Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C (wt.%), were investigated by nano-indentation and DFT calculations to establish the hardness of κ-carbide and B2 intermetallic phases as a function of annealing temperature (500–1050 °C) and Ni addition.

alloys.description: Duplex low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C steel containing 5 wt.% Ni, one of the two grades selected to compare the nanomechanical properties of ordered NiAl-type B2 compounds and the κ-phase (L1'2). Melted in an induction furnace and processed as experimental alloys.
alloys.alloys_notes: Given as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni throughout the abstract, introduction, methods, and results. Tables 1 and 2 label the same alloy as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni (0.5C), which appears to be a typographical inconsistency in the carbon content (0.5 vs 0.8).

source.reason: The abstract (b0008) and Materials section (b0017) explicitly report the two studied alloys as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni and Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C (wt.%), with the Ni-containing grade distinguished by 5 wt.% Ni. Table 2 (b0032) reports the corresponding hardness values per alloy/temperature, using the 0.5C label.

alloys.description: Duplex low-density Ni-free Fe-Mn-Al-C steel, the second grade studied and used as the Ni-free counterpart to compare the behaviour of FeAl-type B2 and needle-like κ-carbides.
alloys.alloys_notes: Given as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C throughout the abstract, introduction, methods, and conclusions. Tables 1 and 2 label the same alloy as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C (0.5C), which appears to be a typographical inconsistency (0.5 vs 0.8 C).

source.reason: b0008 and b0017 explicitly report Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C as the Ni-free grade studied, and b0018/b0022 contrast it with the Ni-containing sample. Table 2 (b0032) reports its hardness values per annealing temperature.

processes.processes_notes: Applied to both alloys (Ni-containing and Ni-free); therefore not tied to a single alloy. Annealing treatments at 500–1050 °C were conducted after this solution treatment.

unmapped_findings: Composition labeling inconsistency: Tables 1 and 2 (b0022, b0032) name the alloys Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni and Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C (0.5C), whereas the abstract, introduction, methods and conclusions (b0008, b0017, b0058) consistently report the C content as 0.8C; the 0.5C table labels appear to be a typographical error.
Annealing holding time for the 500–1050 °C treatments is not explicitly reported in the cleaned text; only the annealing temperatures are given.

Measured precipitate compositions used to rationalize hardness: κ-carbides contained ~18.4 wt.% Mn at 500 °C and ~24.8 wt.% Mn at 700 °C; B2 Al content ranged 22.8–24.6 wt.%; B2 Ni content rose from 8.2 wt.% (500 °C) to 10.1 wt.% (1050 °C).

DFT-calculated elastic properties were obtained for a series of ordered compounds (FeAl, Fe3Al, Fe3AlC, Fe2MnAlC, FeMn2AlC, Mn3AlC, Fe3Al-L12) that are model phases rather than the two experimental steels; these computational compounds are not the alloy research objects of the study.
